statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases from 16 to 15 because the price path continued to mean-revert through the hour. NQ futures were verified at 29,229.00, down 219.75 points or 0.75%, inside a 29,044.25 to 29,508.25 session range, up from 29,196.25 an hour ago. Cash NAS100 at 29,180.33 has recovered off its 29,038.22 opening-auction low, which is now into its third cash hour without a retest, and VIX at 17.23 has eased from 17.65 and sits well below its 18.05 session high. Volatility decaying while price oscillates inside a roughly 210-point cash band is mean reversion functioning, which is the opposite of the no-retracement path this score measures. Working against that, Brent at $107.25 is up about 6.0% and WTI at $101.77 up about 6.0%, both extending to fresh highs since May, the ten-year Treasury yield at 4.93% is up roughly 8 basis points to its highest since October 2023, and the two-year at 4.56% is up about 11 basis points. Semiconductors are broadly weaker while several megacaps hold up, which remains dispersion rather than the aligned amplifier stack a lethal path requires.
recommendation: Tail at 15 maps the policy state to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution false under the fixed repository mapping. The danger window is drawn narrowly around 12:30 to 14:00 UTC on 11 September, widened by thirty minutes from the previous assessment so that it covers the August consumer price release, the first hour of post-release price discovery and the 13:30 UTC U.S. opening auction, since release-plus-opening-auction overlap is the specific combination most associated with persistent intraday extension. Conditional tail reaches 22 in the 12:00 UTC slot tomorrow and 21 in the hour after; those are the only two forward slots mapped to the watch band. A secondary conditional peak of 19 sits in the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots today, covering the U.S. cash close and Oracle's scheduled fiscal Q1 2027 results and 21:00 UTC call into materially thinner futures liquidity. That peak stays inside the low band because thin-book earnings reactions are normally discontinuous gaps rather than sustained one-way paths, and because Oracle is NYSE-listed so its transmission to the Nasdaq-100 runs through software and AI-capex sentiment rather than index weight. Stress holds at 85 and remains extreme: August producer prices at 0.4% on the month and 5.4% on the year with core less foods, energy and trade services at 0.3% and 4.7%, crude extending on Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea escalation, and a 16 September Federal Reserve decision into markets now pricing roughly 63% to 72% odds of a hike depending on the venue are all unresolved. Stress at that level describes the environment and does not on its own move the mapped state past the blocking threshold.
headline: NQ firms to 29,229.00 and VIX eases to 17.23 from its 18.05 high while the 29,038.22 cash low stays untested for a third hour; tail eases from 16 to 15 even as Brent extends to $107.25 and the ten-year holds 4.93%.
body:
The hour resolved last hour's open question in favour of the range. The previous assessment flagged one checkpoint: whether the 29,038.22 cash low would be retested. It was not. NQ futures instead firmed from 29,196.25 to 29,229.00, down 0.75% on the day, and cash NAS100 at 29,180.33 has recovered from the lower half of its 29,038.22 to 29,250.41 session band. Price has now traded in both directions inside a roughly 210-point cash range for more than three hours, and the opening-auction low has held through the whole of it.

The volatility signal moved the same way. VIX printed 18.05 at its session high and 17.65 an hour ago; it is now 17.23, still up 4.7% on the day but decaying. Under the framework used here, tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion for long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach. A held low, repeated two-way rotation and a volatility index rolling off its high are three independent observations pointing the same way, which is why tail steps down to 15 rather than holding at 16.

The cross-asset backdrop did not improve, and that is why the step down is one point rather than several. Brent at $107.25 is up about 6.0% and WTI at $101.77 up about 6.0%, both at their highest since May, after Saudi crude output fell to its lowest level since 1990 and Iran signalled continued retaliatory strikes. The ten-year Treasury yield at 4.93% is up roughly 8 basis points to its highest since October 2023 and the two-year at 4.56% is up about 11 basis points, an unusual combination of an energy shock and a hawkish rates repricing arriving together. Semiconductors are the weak sector, with the main semiconductor ETF off about 1.7%, while several megacaps hold up. That dispersion matters: an aligned amplifier stack across yields, oil, semiconductors, megacaps and breadth is one of the few conditions that historically converts a difficult session into a lethal one, and it is not present.

The scheduled sequence from here is dense. August producer prices printed at 12:30 UTC this morning at 0.4% on the month and 5.4% on the year, with core less foods, energy and trade services at 0.3% and 4.7%; the market absorbed that with a gap lower and then a partial recovery, which is the behaviour assumed for tomorrow's release as well. Oracle reports fiscal Q1 2027 after the bell today with a 21:00 UTC call, and the August consumer price index lands at 12:30 UTC tomorrow, thirty minutes after which pre-market positioning gives way to the 13:30 UTC opening auction. Published expectations centre on roughly 0.4% headline and 0.2% core, with a core print at or above 0.3% widely described as the threshold that would harden the case for a rate increase at the 16 September FOMC meeting.

None of that scheduled density is scored as tail today. Event importance, forecast dispersion and surprise magnitude raise stress and affect confidence; they do not establish that a no-retracement path has formed. The forward window reflects that split: stress stays in the extreme band throughout and peaks at 88 around the release, while tail stays in the low band for twenty-two of twenty-four slots and enters the watch band only for the two hours covering the release and the opening auction that follows it. Confidence is 88, supported by directly verified futures and cash levels, a verified VIX print, verified two-year and ten-year yields, verified Brent and WTI levels, the official producer price release and a re-verified seven-day calendar.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 17:00 UTC on 9 September to 16:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 12 with a mixed read, eases to a 9 to 8 trough across the U.S. close and the first overnight hours, and holds a narrow 9 to 11 band through the Asian and European morning. The regime change sits in the last six slots: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the producer price release printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and a 24 peak at 13:00 UTC covering the opening auction, the only two hours of the window mapped to the watch band. From there the path decays: 17 at 14:00 UTC, 14 at 15:00 UTC and 16 at 16:00 UTC as the recovery stalled short of the session high. Stress rose monotonically across the same span, from 80 overnight to 86 at the release peak and 85 at the close of the window, while confidence never left the high band, dipping only to 84 in the release hour itself. The shape of the window is the argument for the current read: the highest tail values decayed within two hours of the print rather than persisting, which is orderly post-event price discovery.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with the session low still holding and volatility easing, and closes in the U.S. mid-morning after the August consumer price release. Conditional tail starts at 15 in the current 17:00 UTC hour, ticks to 16 and 17 across the crude settlement and the power hour, and reaches an afternoon peak of 19 in the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots covering the U.S. cash close and Oracle's scheduled fiscal Q1 2027 results and call into thin futures liquidity. It then decays through 17 and 14 into the late evening and settles to an 11 floor across the Asian hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. The path rebuilds gradually through the European session, 12 at the cash open and 13 to 14 through the late morning, then 16 in the final hour before the release. The window peak is 22 in the 12:00 UTC slot that contains the 12:30 UTC consumer price index, with 21 in the following hour where post-release repricing overlaps the 13:30 UTC U.S. opening auction. Those two slots are the only ones mapped to the watch band and define the danger window. From 14:00 UTC the path eases through 18, 16 and 15 as the University of Michigan preliminary sentiment lands and the release is assumed absorbed. Stress never leaves the extreme band, running 82 to 86 outside the release and peaking at 88 across the two release hours. Confidence declines from 88 to a 70 to 72 trough around the release purely as a function of forecast distance and binary-outcome uncertainty, not because the current evidence base is thin.
